title: The Concept of Cogito and Cartesian Doubt
text:
Cartesian doubt posits a methodological skepticism, suggesting that certainty must be achieved by questioning all existing beliefs. This process leads to the conclusion encapsulated in the dictum *Cogito ergo sum* (I think, therefore I am), which establishes the existence of consciousness as the one irreducible point of certain knowledge.

This initial realization provides an epistemological anchor from which subsequent truths can theoretically be built. The 'thinking thing'—the conscious self—is identified as existing independently of the physical body or external sensory input, thereby shifting the foundation of knowledge from empiricism toward rationalism.
